newsitem.title: PERU: Peru signs oil and gas contract with U.S. firm.
newsitem.headline: Peru signs oil and gas contract with U.S. firm.

text.p: The Peruvian government signed an contract with the United States' Quintana Minerals Peru LLC to explore and develop block 81 in central Peru, the government daily El Peruano reported.
The government did not give details of the accord but said last month it estimated the contracts it was due to sign in December would each require an investment of around $40 million.

This year, the government has signed ten oil contracts. Energy and Mines Minister Alberto Pandolfi has said Peru hopes to sign a further four contracts before the end of the year, and eight more in 1997.
To date, the government has signed 35 oil contracts with private companies. Twenty are at the exploration stage and 15 are already producing oil.

The government has said the state oil company Perupetro is close to signing contracts involving Peruvian miner Buenaventura, oil giants Royal Dutch/Shell Mobil Corp, Atlantic Richfield Co, and Argentina's Pluspetrol Corp .

A consortium of Shell and Mobil signed a two year contract in May 1996 to appraise the huge Camisea hydrocarbon reserves with a view to developing them. Shell is the operator of the group and majority holder with a 57.5 percent share.

If this oil consortium decides to develop the reserves, the project is likely to last 40 years and become the largest foreign investment commitment in Peru at almost $3 billion, according to the consortium and the government.
